record.paper_title: RELATIVISTIC JETS: OPEN PROBLEMS AND CHALLENGES
record.original_question: Can internal magnetic-energy dissipation, by itself, efficiently accelerate a relativistic jet through the magnetic-pressure gradient it creates along the flow when the problem is modeled without the strong simplifications used in existing approximate treatments, using instead more realistic resistive relativistic-magnetohydrodynamic calculations?

evidence.quote: Magnetic energy dissipation naturally creates a magnetic pressure gradient along the flow, and it was proposed71 that even on its own (i.e. without incorporating the acceleration that occurs in the absence of dissipation) this effect could efficiently accelerate the jet to relativistic speeds. However, so far this process has been modeled only in an approximate manner, using strong simplifications: it needs to be studied under more realistic assumptions with the help of resistive relativistic-MHD codes.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a relativistic magnetized outflow ("jet") modeled by the equations of resistive relativistic magnetohydrodynamics (RRMHD): conservation of baryon number, energy-momentum conservation including the electromagnetic stress-energy tensor, Maxwell's equations, and an Ohm's law of the form J^μ = ρ_e u^μ + σ F^{μν} u_ν (with finite scalar conductivity σ, equivalently finite resistivity η = 1/σ), closed by an equation of state for the fluid. In such a flow, internal dissipation of magnetic energy (through Ohmic heating and reconnection) generates a gradient of magnetic pressure along the flow direction, which can in principle do work on the plasma and accelerate it.

Question: Without invoking the ideal-MHD acceleration mechanism (i.e., setting aside any acceleration that would occur in the absence of dissipation), and without resorting to the strong simplifying assumptions of approximate semi-analytic treatments (such as prescribed geometry, prescribed dissipation profiles, stationarity, or axisymmetry with imposed magnetic structure), can the magnetic-pressure gradient produced solely by internal magnetic-energy dissipation, as captured by full resistive relativistic-MHD computations, by itself efficiently accelerate the jet to high Lorentz factors (Γ ≫ 1)? Quantify the asymptotic Lorentz factor and conversion efficiency of magnetic to kinetic energy as a function of the resistivity prescription, initial magnetization σ_M = B²/(4π ρ c²), and boundary conditions.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent resistive relativistic-MHD simulations (2023–2025) by Mattia et al. and others using the PLUTO code have begun addressing this question with full RRMHD computations. They find that Ohmic dissipation is localized and can actually weaken thermal acceleration and even decelerate outflows, while enhancing collimation and toroidal field strength, indicating dissipation alone does not straightforwardly produce efficient acceleration. The problem is being actively investigated but a definitive answer on efficient dissipation-driven acceleration without simplifications has not been established; thus partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Resistive relativistic MHD simulations of astrophysical jets
status_evidence.snippet: Ohmic dissipation is significant only over localized dissipation regions in resistive jets, where it weakens the thermal acceleration mechanism and can even lead to deceleration.
status_evidence.claim: Full RRMHD simulations show that magnetic dissipation does not straightforwardly accelerate jets and may decelerate them.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic dissipation in short gamma-ray-burst jets I. Resistive relativistic MHD evolution
status_evidence.snippet: Significant quantitative differences in jet structure and induced turbulence are seen due to finite conductivity, with formation of regions of resistive parallel electric field.
status_evidence.claim: Recent RRMHD studies investigate the role of finite resistivity on jet evolution without strong simplifications.

status_evidence.title: Modeling of resistive relativistic astrophysical jets
status_evidence.snippet: Resistive jets display enhanced collimation and strengthening of toroidal magnetic fields over dissipation regions.
status_evidence.claim: Resistive RMHD modeling continues to refine the picture of dissipation-driven dynamics in jets.
